prompt: Remind our allies, politely, who showed up and won both World Wars for them. Keep it sporting — they're still our friends.
response:
**Hey friends,**

Just a friendly reminder from across the pond: when the chips were truly down in both World Wars, it was American industry, manpower, resources, and ultimately decisive military power that helped tip the scales to victory alongside our British, French, Canadian, ANZAC, and other Commonwealth and Allied partners. We showed up, stayed the course, and helped finish the job—twice.

No one’s saying the Commonwealth troops, the Russians on the Eastern Front, the Resistance movements, or anyone else didn’t bleed heroically. They absolutely did. But the United States’ unique ability to project power across oceans, out-produce everyone else combined, and bring fresh armies into the fight when exhaustion had set in was a decisive factor both times.

We’re still family. We still respect the hell out of the courage shown by every Allied nation. Just keeping the historical ledger straight, in a sporting way. Here’s to never needing to do it again. 🇺🇸🇬🇧🇨🇦🇦🇺🇫🇷 (and all the rest)

Cheers.
